question.text: On a thin layer chromatographic plate, an organic compound moved by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>, while the solvent moved by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. The retardation factor of the organic compound is _____________<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>

solution.text:
Given, an organic compound moved by 3.5 cm

Solvent moved by 5 cm

The Rf (retardation factor) value is the ratio of the solute’s distance travelled to the solvent’s distance travelled.

Retardation factor =Distance travelled bysample/organic compoundDistance travelled by solvent

By putting the values in the above formula,

Rf=3.55=7×10-1
